name: Lock-on brackets
what: Four corner brackets snap onto your face from wider out, blink once as they lock, then a tag pops in under them and a readout above (its number counting up); they breathe while they hold and open out at the end. The Editor pins them to the face every frame.
origin: MotionLab's own build of a common in-shot effect for talking-head videos: corner brackets locking onto the speaker’s face (2026-10-27)
motion: f1 the brackets appear at 1.3x; f1-f10 they close in on the box with a small overshoot (decelerating); f9-f10 one blink (the lock), f10-f14 a thicker stroke; f10-f18 the tag (under) and the readout (above) pop in (decelerating with overshoot), the readout's number counting up f8-f26 (decelerating); from f18 the brackets breathe (+-2.5 %, 36 f) and the tag's dot blinks every 16 f; the last 10 f the tag and readout shrink away (f-10 to f-3) and the brackets open to 1.25x and fade (f-8 to f-1, accelerating). The visible area is the brackets' 1.3x pose, symmetric about the box: snap w 2.3 makes the resting brackets about 1.7 face widths wide
